points.description: States that a static array is initialized only once (not every time the function runs or is entered), so the initialization is not repeated on later calls.
points.partial_credit: Half marks (2) for stating that a static array keeps its values or is initialized once, without making clear the initialization is not repeated; or for a vague statement about static arrays being initialized differently.

points.description: States that this one-time initialization happens when the function is called (the first time the function is called).

rubric.notes: Full marks (5) for stating that a static array is initialized only once, when the function is first called, and not on later calls. Part marks go to a statement that is half right, such as saying static arrays are initialized once without saying that this is not repeated, or a vague remark about static arrays being initialized differently. Answers that only describe non-static arrays, or talk about scope or memory without stating the one-time initialization, earn no marks. Extra correct detail, such as the array keeping its values between calls, is fine and does not cost marks.
